title: Security in the user experience: disclosure, reporting and refusals

videos.script: Every defence so far ran on Tarefa's servers. The client saw none of them. They saw a chat window, a reply, a refusal and a confirmation. {{title}} So the screens get rules too. The welcome says the client is talking to an automated assistant, and offers a person. {{disclosure}} Every reply can be reported, because the client sees the replies no check caught. {{report}} A refusal says why and what to do next. Something went wrong, try again, does neither, and turns a limit into a loop. {{refusal}} A confirmation shows the account, the job and the amount. Without them, the person confirming checks nothing. {{confirm}} Then a week of reports. One prompt version drew thirty reports per thousand calls, the other two. {{reports}} Read one at a time, they looked like odd days. Counted by version, they were one change nobody reviewed. {{version}}
